newsitem.title: USA: Texan whose case led to landmark dissent executed.
newsitem.headline: Texan whose case led to landmark dissent executed.

text.p: A Texas killer, whose 1994 appeal to the U.S. Supreme Court rekindled the debate over capital punishment, was executed by lethal injection on Wednesday at the state prison here.

The third of four men executed in Texas this week, Bruce Callins, 37, was put to death for killing a Fort Worth man during the 1980 armed robbery of a topless bar where his girlfriend worked as a dancer, prosecutors said.

"I want to let all my people know and everybody who is here and has supported me know that I love them and wish them all the best," Callins said before he was injected with a lethal dose of chemicals and died shortly before 7:30 p.m. EDT (2330 GMT).

Callins' case became a rallying cry for opponents of capital punishment after Supreme Court Justice Harry Blackmun in a landmark dissent said the death penalty was "fraught with arbitrariness, discrimination, caprice, and mistake."

In the dissent, published a few months before he retired from the bench, Blackmun said he regretted the Supreme Court's decision to reinstate the death penalty in a 1976 case in which he voted with the majority.

"From this day forward, I no longer shall tinker with the machinery of death," Blackmun wrote. "I feel morally and intellectually obligated simply to concede that the death penalty experiment has failed."

Citing Blackmun's dissent, the American Bar Association in February called for an immediate halt to executions in the United States. Twenty years after the Supreme Court reinstated the death penalty, the lawyers' group said the appeals process was "seriously flawed" and the sentence discriminated against blacks and other minorities.
Blackmun's office said he would have no comment on Callins' execution.

Callins, who was black, was convicted of murdering Allen Huckleberry as he held up a nearly empty topless bar on a June afternoon in 1980. After threatening to "shoot anyone who held anything back," Callins shot Huckleberry in the neck when he was slow to hand over his wallet, prosecutors said.

Callins had been on the Texas death row since July 1982, and received four stays of his execution before a final round of appeals were rejected by a state appeals court and the Supreme Court earlier this month.

His execution was the 14th in Texas this year and the 121st since executions resumed in Texas in 1982. Texas leads the nation in the number of executions since the Supreme Court reinstated capital punishment. More than 330 people have been executed since the death penalty was restored.
With 10 more executions scheduled for June, Texas is set by mid-year to eclipse 1995's record 19 executions in a year, prison officials said.
